title: Crisp SVG Icons

body_html:
I’ve been using icon-fonts for many years. There’s great browser-support, even IE5.5 is supposed to support them!

But on my newest project, I ditched them, and went for SVG-icons. Why?

First of all, it’s much easier to edit SVG, it’s XML-markup. A font needs to be recompiled/rewritten, and for full browser-support, a lot of different formats are needed.

When a font fails to load, the character-value of the font is displayed instead. So, if the character for a Home-icon is “H” and the font fails to load, the user will see this:

HHome

Not cool.

Secondly, it’s possible to create something similar to an image sprite with SVG, using the <symbol>-tag. Using this technique, only one request is needed for all svg-icons on a site.

SVG “Sprite” using <symbol>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">
  <symbol id="ico_favorites" viewBox="0 0 48 48">
    <path d="M35.1,43L24,36L13,43.1c-1.4,0.9-2.2,0.3-1.8-1.3l3.3-12.7L4.3,20.8c-1.3-1-1-2,0.7-2.1l13.1-0.8l4.8-12.2 c0.6-1.5,1.6-1.5,2.2,0l4.8,12.2L43,18.6c1.7,0.1,2,1,0.7,2.1L33.5,29l3.4,12.7C37.3,43.3,36.5,43.9,35.1,43z" />
  </symbol>

  <symbol id="ico_search" viewBox="0 0 48 48">
  ... etc.
  </symbol>
</svg>

If the code above were to be saved to a file named icons.svg under a folder called svg, the following syntax is used to embed an icon:

<svg><use xlink:href="svg/icons.svg#ico_favorites"></use></svg>

There are pros and cons using this method. Mostly pros!
When using inline SVG you can style the individual paths using CSS — unfortunately, this is not possible using <symbol>, as discussed here.

However, you can still use fill on <symbol> which was all you could using font-icons, so …

My favourite icon-font-provider, IcoMoon, have already added Export to SVG/Symbol-functionality, so the switch from icon-fonts to SVG is easier than ever!

So sensiTive

Tip! SVG is caseSensitive, so it’s viewBox instead of viewbox — I learned this the hard way!

And finally …

To make all this work in other browsers than Chrome (for the moment!), you need to add a small JavaScript: Svg4Everybody.

Happy coding!
